implementation: Independent receipt-driven Roll X controller/renderer, original code-generated graphics/audio and partial integer payout evaluator. No old game or provider source code reused.

mechanics.statement: Before a round, the player chooses a bet and a target multiplier.
The wheel stops on a green winning sector or empty losing sector.
Observed green rounds return bet multiplied by the chosen target; the returned amount includes the stake. Empty-sector observations return zero.
mechanics.equation: totalPayoutMinor = betMinor * targetBps / 10000 for green; 0 for empty
mechanics.restriction: Only integral minor-unit products and observed 1.4x/2x targets are accepted by the fixture evaluator.

unpublishedEvidence.reason: Roll X own-bet history panel intentionally excluded from public GitHub evidence; private original preserved unchanged.

mechanics.statement: The official product page advertises up to 30x.
The in-game mathematics panel displays RTP 96% and says player speed/skill does not determine outcomes.
mechanics.restriction: No RNG distribution, winning-sector probability, hidden tables or independent-engine RTP is thereby established.

mechanics.statement: During the extra manual control round, SPIN changed to STOP; clicking STOP was followed by one settled history row with bet 0.5 DMO, chosen 2x, payout 1 DMO.
mechanics.restriction: This observation alone does not prove the provider's internal result-selection timing. The new engine must preserve the accepted financial outcome independently of STOP.

mechanics.statement: AUTO offers 10, 50, 100, 500 or 1000 rounds, target/bet fields, and stop thresholds for a single win or balance decrease/increase.
mechanics.testedBehavior: 10 selected; one additional settled round; AUTO cancelled and total history count stayed eight before the subsequent manual round.

mechanics.statement: No bonus or free-spin mechanic was observed in this session or described in the captured six-panel help.
mechanics.restriction: Do not add an invented bonus mechanic or describe absence as a defect.

controls.implementation: Editable bet and target fields use current server bet levels and verified target subset; all confirmed AUTO rounds bind the selected pair. Invalid/stale selections are rejected before mutation or a request.

stateContract.source: New implementation requirements; observations inform presentation only.
transitions: Read existing account/session and game availability; no new wager.
Only an authorized injected isolated fixture can currently enable play; default production wrapper remains UNAVAILABLE.
Freeze bet and target; submit one adapter action.
Missing receipt keeps original request pending, locks wager controls and stops AUTO.
Validate and retain accepted immutable receipt before drawing outcome.
Retrieve accepted receipt with original request, restore its accepted bet/target and keep AUTO stopped.
Finish receipt presentation; STOP and Turbo change only this timing.
Read current account balance separately from historical receipt; only continue if transport ready.
Accepted receipt retained if account refresh fails; no replacement wager.
Dispose owned request callbacks, animation, audio and AUTO delays on actual exit.
requirements: Use the existing project wallet and recovery adapter; no detached balance or ledger.
Pause AUTO whenever a prior request or connectivity is unresolved.
Retain requestId, roundId, accepted target, rules version and engine version.
A refresh/second tab must retrieve accepted state before permitting another wager.
For exit with an accepted unresolved round, preserve recoverable identifiers; do not synthesize a refund.
Provider help's disconnect sentence describes source behavior but does not authorize inventing a settlement amount in ZPLAY.

lifecycle.hiddenTab: Stop AUTO, finish presentation, cut/suspend audio.
lifecycle.bfcacheHide: Pause without disposing; keep recovery identity and listeners.
lifecycle.bfcacheShow: Resume with account refresh and pending-round guard; do not restart AUTO.
lifecycle.actualExit: Dispose session, renderer, audio, handlers and timers.
